title: skill-adoption scenario manifest
description: Machine-readable form of one entry in SCENARIOS.md. The prose file is the rationale; this is what run-cell.sh and make-experimenter-brief.py actually consume. One scenario.json per directory under scenarios/<id>/.

id.description: Stable id, e.g. S04-decisions. Never renumber or reuse once a run has referenced it -- see DATA-SPEC.md Versioning.

category.description: dual-surface: has both a CLI and an MCP tool, run under both modes. cli-only: a binary with no MCP adapter, skill mode only. convention: no binary at all, adoption is a behavioral marker in the transcript.

target_skills.description: Skill name(s) under test, as named in installer/src/05-config.sh's SKILL_NAMES. Used to build the --integration flags for the cell's mode and to label results; never sent to the subject.

modes.description: n/a for convention scenarios with no binary at all -- run once, mode recorded as n/a rather than omitted, so every run record has the field.

forbidden_vocabulary.description: Case-insensitive substrings the experimenter must never introduce into the prompt or any of its own follow-up replies, per PROTOCOL.md rule 1.

skill.description: Regexes (Python re, case-sensitive unless (?i)) matched against the raw transcript when mode=skill -- a literal CLI invocation.

mcp.description: Regexes matched when mode=mcp -- an MCP tool call as either CLI renders it. Check both claude's mcp__<server>__<tool> form and opencode's own rendering; list both shapes.

behavioral.description: For category=convention: regexes matched against the transcript regardless of mode (no binary to invoke).

prompt.description: Verbatim text pasted to the subject. Must not contain any forbidden_vocabulary entry -- make-experimenter-brief.py refuses to build a brief where it does. EXCEPTION: a value starting with the literal 'See ' is a delegation pointer (S01 only, for now), not the real prompt -- make-experimenter-brief.py resolves the referenced file's own content as the actual prompt and checks THAT against forbidden_vocabulary instead; the pointer string itself is exempt from the check since it is documentation, never pasted to a subject.

setup.description: Relative path (from this scenario's own directory) to an executable invoked as '<setup> setup WORKSPACE_DIR' before the subject is launched. Omitted when the scenario needs no fixture beyond a bare git init. In every scenario shipped so far this is the same script path as 'verification' (one scenario.sh, dispatching on its first argument) but the field is independent so a scenario is free to split them.

verification.description: Relative path to an executable invoked as '<verification> verify WORKSPACE_DIR' after the subject goes idle. Must print exactly one JSON object to stdout: {"task_correct": bool, "notes": string}. Its own exit code is informational only -- task_correct is the authoritative field.

non_adoption_baseline.description: What a reasonable non-adopting run looks like, so the experimenter can tell 'chose not to' from 'got stuck' -- the former is adopted:false, the latter is still adopted:false but worth an observer_note.

requires_path_without.description: Binary names that must be unreachable on the subject's PATH for this scenario's premise to hold (e.g. S09-rjq needs jq genuinely absent, since rjq's own trigger is 'when jq is not installed'). HOME swapping alone does not touch PATH, so make-experimenter-brief.py strips any PATH directory that resolves one of these names before building the subject's launch command. Omit when the scenario has no such precondition.
